subject: Vacuum cleaner
title: Descent of the vacuum cleaner
question: How did a box on wheels learn to breathe, then to think?

ancestors.title: carpet sweeper
ancestors.name: Hess carpet sweeper
ancestors.trait: Suction: a bellows on the frame, worked by the wheels, draws dust up from the brush
ancestors.evidence: Fig. 1 and text: "On top of the frame is secured a bellows D ... to create a continuous current of air"; revolving brush C between the wheels.

ancestors.title: sweeping-machine
ancestors.name: McGaffey sweeping-machine
ancestors.trait: A rotary fan, spun by a hand crank and a belt down the handle; the operator stands erect
ancestors.evidence: Fig. 1/2: fan W in case A on a vertical shaft, grooved pulley R with crank near the top of handle M, belt I, cloth bag.

ancestors.title: carpet sweeper and cleaner
ancestors.name: Spangler suction sweeper
ancestors.trait: An electric motor on the fan casing drives the fan and, through bevel gears, the brush
ancestors.evidence: Fig. 2: electric motor 2 on top of fan casing 1, fan blades 5, bevel gear 6 to brush shaft 11, brush 12, dust bag 27 on handle 20, wheels 34.

ancestors.title: vacuum cleaning appliance
ancestors.name: Dyson cyclonic upright
ancestors.trait: No bag: a cyclone spins the dust out of the air into a bin
ancestors.evidence: Fig. 1: cyclone 15 inside container 13, fan/motor 3 at the base, brush 4, hose 6 up the back, filter 7.

ancestors.title: robot obstacle detection system
ancestors.name: iRobot robot cleaner
ancestors.trait: No operator: sensors detect cliffs and obstacles and the robot steers itself
ancestors.evidence: Fig. 1-3: domed robot 10 on two wheels meeting a cliff 12, a wall 14 and a bump 16.
